Theorem
[Representation formula] ↗ def:fundamental-solution-laplace ↗ thm:liouville-theorem-harmonic 1. ch2:2.2-thm-9\group Harmonic Functions

Let $n\ge 3$ and $f\in C_c^2(\R ^n)$. Every bounded solution of $-\Delta u=f$ on $\R ^n$ has the form \[ u(x)=\int _{\R ^n}\Phi (x-y)f(y)\, dy+C \] for a constant $C$.
Proof

\sketch Since $\Phi (x)\to 0$ as $|x|\to \infty $, the convolution is a bounded solution. Its difference from any other bounded solution is bounded and harmonic, hence constant by Liouville’s theorem.

□
